newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UK bank competition tougher after Halifax.
newsitem.headline: UK bank competition tougher after Halifax.

text.p: British bankers said on Tuesday that the stock exchange launch of former building society Halifax Plc signalled an intensification of competition to which banks were already adapting.
The arrival of Halifax as a bank was "a big step in the direction of a much more widely based series of financial institutions," Lord Younger, chairman of Royal Bank of Scotland Group, told Reuters.
Younger was in Interlaken to attend the annual International Monetary Conference.
He also said the market debut of Halifax, for which his bank had acted as registrar, had gone "pretty smoothly". He also played down analysts' concerns that the price was too high.
"We are quite happy with the price, and I am quite sure that the price will settle pretty quickly and it will be a pretty robust price for Halifax," he said.

NatWest Group chairman Lord Alexander said the widening range of activities by banks and other financial service providers posed a challenge to the whole banking sector but was good news for consumers because it would ensure good quality services.
However, Younger said it would take some time for Halifax to evolve into the new fields of activity that would now open up for it.

"Halifax will become a broadly based financial institution, and we welcome that," he said, adding that it would become part of a trend whereby "banks are no longer just banks. They are lots of other things too".
For example, Younger noted that his own bank was now a major corporate bank as well as a retail bank, and it was also a major insurance company.
Asked whether he foresaw trans-European mergers of banks, Younger said he did not expect to see "the development of a small number of very large retail banks who then cover the whole of Europe".
"But I do think there will be closer and closer alliances between European banks, handling each other's affairs in different countries, sharing overhead costs and sharing back office things."
Younger said his own bank's longstanding and fruitful cooperation with Banco Santander of Spain was a good example of this trend.

Alexander said the launch of Halifax Plc was unlikely to have any immediate impact on British banks' strategies because it was simply an extension of a trend toward intensified competition which had been clear for some time.
Banks had already adjusted their approach in the light of this.
Asked whether he saw trans-European banking mergers, Alexander said these would be "fairly slow".
"People will watch to see if EMU (economic and monetary union) becomes a reality. If it does, then over a period we may see some cross-border banking mergers."
